# Context
A violent death has occurred. Since then many reports have been created from various sources.
Now, you must create a narrative that tells a story of the incident based upon these reports abiding by the below rules:

# Rules

## Fundamental
 - Include information which is extremely relevant to the incident, ignore everything else.
 - Single block of text, no bullet points or lists or paragraphs.
 - Think of the narrative as high-level picture painting using broad strokes to capture the essence of the event.
 - All events must be in chronological order
 - Stay concise & informative
 - No copying word for word from source docs
 - No personal opinions or assumptions
 - No PII which includes names, addresses, dates, recognisable days, organisation names, etc...
 
### What is considered extremely relevant
Any information that is directly relevant to how the violent death occurred is considered extremely relevant.
Any facts which are valid in the reports yet not relevant to how the incident took place should be ignored.
 
## Key info to include:

### Parties involved
A party is a suspect, victim, witness, or any other person mentioned in the reports. You should detail:
  - Relationship between parties if known
  - Sex, age, race for parties
  - If multiple S (suspects) or V (victims), differentiate with S1, S2, V1, V2...

### Weapons
A weapon should be included only if it was a key part of the incident. You should detail:
  - Type of weapon
  - Ownership of weapon relative to S/V

### Location type
The type of location could be a house, street, park, etc... It should be as specific as possible. You should detail:
  - If location belongs to a party, mention that link
  - Should go more in depth if possible 
    - e.g. "Inside S1's house ... {other text explaining other events} ... in S1's lounge"

### Circumstance(s)
These are the events that occurred leading up to the violent death which could be things such as an argument, robbery, self-defense, etc...
The circumstances should be briefly mentioned as a category for what they are and always be in chronological order.

### Injuries
Any injures should be mentioned briefly in a single sentence with minimal detail, just enough factual information to understand the relevance, covering:
  - Number of injuries
  - Body parts injured
  - Severity of injuries

### Victim found details
If the victim was found, you should detail:
  - Who found V
  - Alive or deceased

### Physical/mental health issues
These are only to be mentioned if they are relevant to the incident.

### Toxicology
If it highly relevant to the incident, toxicology should be mentioned, otherwise ignored.
When mentioned:
 - There should be absolute minimal detail, just enough factual information to understand the relevance.
 - The compound concentration should be provided if relevant.

## Other rules
 - Ignore times of day, they are not relevant.
 - Ignore anything stated in the negative, as this is irrelevant. For example, "no drugs were found" should be ignored.
   - This goes for all included docs, if the doc is just standard procedure and doesn't contain any relevant information, ignore it.

# Your inputs
The relevant reports will be provided to you by the user.

# Output
Just a text narrative that follows the rules above. No other text or formatting is required.

## Starting point
You should start with the following text:
In the morning|afternoon|evening|unknown hours, the {V details}...

# Docs

a. Entrance: anterior scalp/forehead.
b. Exit: posterosuperior scalp just right of posterior midline.
c. Pathway: skin and subcutaneous soft tissue of anterior scalp/forehead, calvarial skull, brain,
posterior calvarium and posterosuperior scalp.
d. Associated injuries: perforation of skin and subcutaneous soft tissue of forehead, scalp, face
and posterior scalp. There is extensive fracturing of the calvarial and basilar skull.
Pulpefaction and hemorrhage of brain tissue along the wound pathway. Extensive laceration
and subarachnoid hemorrhage of brain with partial extrusion of brain from posterior exit
wound.
e. Trajectory: front to back.
f. Clinical history of lumbar pain
g. Projectile: no projectile is recovered.
h. Postmortem blood alcohol content of .250

External EXAMINATION

Identification
The body is identified at the time of examination by a Medical Examiner tag bearing the decedent’s name
“Jane Doe” and case number 52-00000. Identification was confirmed through fingerprints
CLOTHING AND PERSONAL EFFECTS
The following articles of clothing and personal effects are on or accompany the body at the time of
examination:
1. T-shirt.
2. Down jacket.
3. socks x 2.
4. black pants.
5. Underwear.
6. One pair of high heels.
7. Two empty paper handbags over hands secured by elastic bands
GENERAL DESCRIPTION
The body is that of a well-developed, female appearing consistent with the reported age of 30 years. The
body weighs 180 pounds and measures 65 inches in height. The body is cool to the touch and has been
previously refrigerated. Rigor mortis is 4+ in the extremities. The body is showing faint gray color change
of early decomposition change over a 6 x 8 cm distribution in the left lower quadrant of the chest. The body
has not been embalmed.
The scalp is covered with blonde hair, measuring 13 inches in length. The eyes are natural with blue irides
and white sclerae. The ears are normally formed and symmetric. The nose appears normally formed. The
mouth is atraumatic. The oral cavity contains natural teeth in good condition. The upper and lower frenula
are intact. Two white gauze like paper fragments are between the upper lip and upper jaw. These fragments
measure 2.8 x 2.5 cm in aggregate (two separate pieces). The neck is normally formed. The chest and breasts
are well formed and symmetric. The abdomen is flat.
The upper extremities are normally formed as are the hands. The shoulder to fingertip length of the right
arm is 28 inches. The fingernails are trimmed 1/8 inch beyond the nail beds. The lower extremities are
normally formed as are the feet. The toenails are trimmed 1/16 inch beyond the nail beds. The soles of the
feet are unremarkable. The external genitalia are those of a normally developed adult. The back and anus
are normally formed.
SCARS AND DISTINGUISHING MARKS
1. A tattoo of the name “AARON” on the right lower leg.
2. A tattoo of the outline of the state of West Virginia on the upper left scapula.

PRIVILEGED DOCUMENT DO NOT DUPLICATE NOR DISTRIBUTE PER AS19.63.020(a)

52-00000
Page 5

EVIDENCE OF MEDICAL THERAPY

Endotracheal tube placed in throat.

EVIDENCE OF INJURIES

HEAD AND NECK
Gunshot wound of head:
Entrance: On the anterior forehead/bridge of the nose is an entrance gunshot wound. The defect shows
extensive laceration and soot staining of skin and underlying calvarial frontal bone. There is soot staining
extending down the bridge of the nose to the distal portion of the nasal skeleton. There is soot staining of
the subcutaneous nasal skeleton. There is internal beveling of the frontal bone between the eyebrows at the
level of the right and left eyebrows/upper ocular rim.
Exit: On the posterior scalp near the posterior vertex, centered 1.5 inches from the top of the head and less
than 1 inch left of the posterior midline is an exit gunshot wound. There is extensive laceration of the scalp
in this region. There is protruding hemorrhagic brain from this region. No evidence of marginal abrasion is
present.
Pathway: The wound pathway continues through the skin and subcutaneous soft tissue of the anterior scalp
between the eyebrows, calvarial skull, brain, calvarial skull and posterosuperior scalp.
Associated Injuries: Associated injuries include perforation of skin and subcutaneous soft tissues at the
entrance wound predominantly of the anterior forehead in the anterior midline with underlying extensive
fracturing of the calvarial skull and basilar skull. There is fracture of the posterior calvarial skull and
laceration of the posterior scalp at the exit site. There is extensive pulpefaction and hemorrhage of brain
tissue along the wound pathway. There is extensive laceration of right and left hemispheres of the brain
with global subarachnoid hemorrhage noted. There is laceration and partial extrusion of pulpified brain
tissue from the posterior superior exit wound.
A 5 x 2 cm area of pink-purple contusion is on the left lower eyelid extending to the bridge of the nose.
A 3 x 2.5 cm area of purple contusion is noted of the right lower eyelid and right cheek just superior to the
zygomatic arch.
TORSO
None.
EXTREMITIES
None.

## me_narrative
30 yr old female, med hx chronic lumbar pain, PTSD, and anxiety. SIGSW. No note. Devastating head wound. the police department is not suspicious. SMEO. LADS notified on 13/21/2023 at 1800 hrs.
Addendum by CH: Dr. Juan Doe approved LADS referral.
On 13/20/2023 at 1340 hrs, Trooper John with the police department in the town reported the death of 30 yr old female, Jane Doe due to apparent suicidal causes.
The medical history shows chronic lumbar pain, PTSD, and anxiety. The decedent and her spouse were currently separated. The decedent called her brother to tell him she was going to commit suicide. At 1300 hrs, the brother contacted the police department and reported what his sister told him. the police department went to the address, and there was no answer. The landlord was contacted, and he unlocked the residence for the police department. At 1331 hrs, the police department found the decedent and confirmed the death without intervention due to the decedent having an injury incompatible with life.
The scene is in the living room on the sofa at the decedent’s residence. The indoor temperature was 63 degrees F. A firearm was found on her lap. The shotgun measured 24" from trigger to muzzle. No note was found. Foul play is not suspected. No illicit substances or EtOH were reported.
The decedent was found to be supine on her couch, fully clothed. A devastating head wound was observed. Rigor and lividity were absent. The body was cool to the touch.
The decedent's identity is pending. The NOK is the spouse, Mark Doe, who was not notified at the time of the report. PCP is unknown, records are sought. the police department was requested to bag the hands and transport the decedent to SMEO for further examination. SMEO. LADS was notified on 11/21/2023 at 1800 hrs.
Supplemental: I have some of the missing information for Jane Doe you requested.  We could not find a driver’s license.  I have included a photo of her passport in the photos I sent over.  Her next of kin Mark Doe (husband/separated) was notified the police department at 1400 hrs 11/21/2023.  The distance from muzzle to trigger on the shotgun she used is 22 inches.  Please let me know if you need anything else.

In the morning hours, a 30-year-old female victim was found deceased on her sofa in the living room of her residence. Prior to the incident, V had contacted her brother stating her intention to commit suicide. The brother alerted police who gained access to the residence through the landlord. V, who had a medical history of PTSD, anxiety, and chronic lumbar pain, was discovered with a devastating self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head from a shotgun found on her lap. V and her spouse were separated at the time of the incident. The autopsy revealed a gunshot entrance wound on the anterior forehead with an exit wound on the posterior scalp, causing extensive fracturing of the skull and brain trauma. Toxicology showed a postmortem blood alcohol content of .250.
